summary: Ustaz Azlan opens the new Hijri year with two reflections: the deed most beloved to Allah is the constant one, however small (illustrated by the book Slow Productivity), and the encouragement to fast in Muharram including Ashura. He then explains why Quraysh saw the Prophet's SAW call as a threat (idols, trade security and the caste system) and the first strategies of persecution: emotional pressure on the companions including Sa'd ibn Abi Waqqas and his mother, Mus'ab ibn Umayr, Umar's pay policy, Abu Jahl's tactics of disrupting merchants and torturing slaves, the ban on reciting the Quran in public, propaganda to discredit it, and An-Nadr ibn Al-Harith's attempt to distract with entertainment.
keyPoints: The deed most beloved to Allah is the constant one, however small; do fewer things, work at a natural pace and focus on quality.
Muharram is the month of Allah and the best fast after Ramadan; fasting Ashura and Tasu'a is sunnah.
Quraysh felt threatened because the call endangered the elite's power, trade security and the caste system.
Sa'd faced his mother's hunger strike; Luqman 14-15 teaches kindness to parents but no obedience in sin.
Abu Jahl led campaigns of disrupting companions' businesses, torturing slaves and banning public recitation of the Quran.
Campaigns to discredit the Quran and distract with entertainment were answered by verses in Al-Furqan and Luqman.
Quraysh leaders secretly listened to the Prophet SAW at night yet refused out of tribal rivalry.

lessons.title: Constancy beats quantity
lessons.body: The most beloved deed is the constant one, however small.

lessons.title: Fewer commitments, higher quality
lessons.body: Do fewer things, work at a natural pace and obsess over quality against the culture of excess productivity.

lessons.title: Fast more in Muharram
lessons.body: Fasting Muharram is best after Ramadan, including Ashura.

lessons.title: A rebuke in revelation shows the Prophet's SAW honesty
lessons.body: The Prophet SAW did not hide verses that rebuked him.

lessons.title: Be good to parents even if they differ in faith
lessons.body: Do not obey in shirk but stay kind; do not abandon family on embracing Islam.

lessons.title: No obedience to a creature in sin
lessons.body: A rule that applies everywhere including the home.

lessons.title: Honour those who sacrificed first
lessons.body: Umar differentiated pay for the earliest to embrace Islam.

lessons.title: Bans do not stop the truth
lessons.body: Bans often raise attention and enthusiasm for the message.

lessons.title: Beware propaganda and out-of-context verses
lessons.body: Today's Islamophobic tactics resemble Quraysh's diversion.

lessons.title: Start with the sirah
lessons.body: Knowing the Prophet's SAW character is a shield against mockery.

lessons.title: Do not point fingers at hypocrites
lessons.body: Umar worried about himself; we should worry about ourselves.

lessons.title: Scrupulousness and self-reckoning
lessons.body: The companions feared that worldly ease would reduce their reward; we may enjoy provision without heedlessness.

dalil.context: The basis of the new year's resolve: be constant even if little.
dalil.translation: The deed most beloved to Allah is the one that is constant even if it is small.

dalil.context: Muharram is called the month of Allah.
dalil.translation: The best fast after Ramadan is the fast in Allah's month, Muharram.

dalil.context: The basis of fasting Ashura and Tasu'a.
dalil.translation: The Prophet SAW saw the Jews fasting on the 10th of Muharram because Musa was saved; he said 'we are closer to Musa,' commanded the fast and intended to add the 9th next year.

dalil.context: The early command to warn kin, referred to in the recap. (reference identified, verse number not stated)
Surah Al-Masad came down after Abu Lahab insulted the Prophet SAW. (reference identified, verse number not stated)
dalil.translation: May the hands of Abu Lahab be ruined! May he be ruined too!

dalil.context: Allah's rebuke when the Prophet SAW frowned at Abdullah ibn Umm Maktum. (reference identified, verse number not stated)
Allah commands kindness to parents and gratitude to Him and them.
dalil.translation: We have commanded people to be good to their parents: their mothers carried them, with strain upon strain, and it takes two years to wean them. Give thanks to Me and to your parents- all will return to Me.

dalil.context: Do not obey if parents force shirk, but keep company with them kindly in this world.
dalil.translation: If they strive to make you associate with Me anything about which you have no knowledge, then do not obey them. Yet keep their company in this life according to what is right, and follow the path of those who turn to Me. You will all return to Me in the end, and I will tell you everything that you have done.

dalil.context: The disbelievers accuse the Quran of being a fabrication helped by others.
dalil.translation: The disbelievers say, ‘This can only be a lie he has forged with the help of others’––they themselves have done great wrong and told lies––

dalil.context: The accusation that the Quran is old tales written down and recited morning and evening.
dalil.translation: and they say, ‘It is just ancient fables, which he has had written down: they are dictated to him morning and evening.’

dalil.context: The reply: it was sent down by Him who knows the secrets of heaven and earth.
dalil.translation: Say, ‘It was sent down by Him who knows the secrets of the heavens and earth. He is all forgiving, all merciful.’

dalil.context: They question why the messenger eats and walks in the markets.
dalil.translation: They also say, ‘What sort of messenger is this? He eats food and walks about in the marketplaces! Why has no angel been sent down to help him with his warnings?

dalil.context: The verse on those who buy idle entertainment to mislead, referring to An-Nadr ibn Al-Harith.
dalil.translation: But there is the sort of person who pays for distracting tales, intending, without any knowledge, to lead others from God’s way, and to hold it up to ridicule. There will be humiliating torment for him!

dalil.context: Why Abdullah ibn Mas'ud was bold enough to recite in public.
dalil.translation: Whoever wants to hear the Quran recited as it was revealed, let him listen to Ibn Umm Abd.
